questions.question: Which South-East Asian country declared a food security emergency to curb soaring rice prices in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Philippines.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **The Philippines declared a food security emergency on rice prices to stabilize the soaring cost of the staple grain.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Agriculture Secretary Francisco Tiu Laurel authorized the release of rice buffer stocks from the National Food Authority (NFA).**
 
• **The Rice Tariffication Law empowers the Agriculture Secretary to declare a food security emergency.**
 
• **Philippines' rice inflation surged to 21.4% in December 2023, prompting intervention.**
 
• **The country’s GDP grew by 5.6% in 2024, below the 6-6.5% target, due to extreme weather events and geopolitical challenges.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National Food Authority (NFA)**__: The agency responsible for maintaining rice buffer stocks to stabilize market prices.
 
• __**Rice Tariffication Law**__: Enacted in **2019**, it allows the government to impose tariffs on rice imports instead of quantitative restrictions.
 
• __**Economic Impact**__: The Philippines ranked as the **third-fastest growing economy in the region**, despite falling short of GDP targets.
 
• __**Climate Challenges**__: The country faced **six typhoons between October and November 2024**, severely affecting agricultural output.

questions.question: What is the primary objective of the **Jan Vishwas Bill 2.0** introduced in the Union Budget 2025-26?

options.text: To decriminalize over 100 provisions across various laws to improve ease of doing business.
To establish a legal framework for increasing foreign direct investment (FDI) limits.
To introduce a new tax rebate scheme for small businesses and MSMEs.
To provide financial assistance to first-time entrepreneurs from marginalized communities.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To decriminalize over 100 provisions across various laws to improve ease of doing business.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **The **Jan Vishwas Bill 2.0** was introduced in the Union Budget 2025-26 to decriminalize over 100 provisions across different laws to facilitate ease of doing business.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• The bill aims to reduce legal burdens on businesses by **removing imprisonment clauses for minor economic offenses** and replacing them with monetary penalties.
 
• The reforms cover laws related to **commerce, trade, finance, corporate governance, and industry regulations.**
 
• It strengthens **India’s business environment, reduces litigation, and promotes investor confidence.**
 
• The initiative aligns with the government's efforts to improve **ease of doing business rankings and foster economic growth.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Jan Vishwas Bill 2.0 Key Features**__

 __
 
• Targets over **100 legal provisions** spread across different business-related laws.
 
• Reduces the **criminalization of minor regulatory offenses.**
 
• Encourages **simplified compliance and faster grievance redressal.**
 
 
 
• **Government's Ease of Doing Business Initiatives**__
 __
 
• Introduction of **Single Window Clearance** for industries.
 
• Digitization of licensing and tax filing processes.
 
• Expansion of the **Investment Friendliness Index** to rank states on business climate.
 
 
 
• **Impact on the Indian Economy**__
 
 
• Boosts **entrepreneurial activity** by removing excessive penalties.
 
• Encourages **startups and MSMEs** by reducing legal risks.
 
• Enhances **foreign investor confidence** in India's regulatory environment.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about **World Wetlands Day 2025**:

 
• The theme for World Wetlands Day 2025 is ‘Protecting Wetlands for our Common Future’.
 
• The celebration of World Wetlands Day 2025 was held at the Parvati Arga Ramsar Site in Gonda, Uttar Pradesh.
 
• The Amrit Dharohar initiative was launched in 2023 to promote the unique conservation values of the Ramsar Sites in India.

Which of the above statements is/are ***INCORRECT***?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**None of them**____**.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **The theme for World Wetlands Day 2025, ‘Protecting Wetlands for our Common Future’, focuses on the importance of wetlands in environmental conservation and sustainable livelihoods.**

 
 
• **​**Hence, Statement 1 is CORRECT.
 
 
 
• **The event was held at the Parvati Arga Ramsar Site in Gonda, Uttar Pradesh, where significant discussions and initiatives regarding wetland conservation took place.**
 
 
• **​**​Hence, Statement 2 is CORRECT.
 
 
 
• **The Amrit Dharohar initiative was launched in 2023 to promote the unique conservation values of Ramsar Sites in India while supporting local livelihoods and generating employment opportunities.**
 
 
• **​**​Hence, Statement 3 is CORRECT.
 
 
 
• **Therefore, none of the statements are INCORRECT.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• Two bird sanctuaries in Tamil Nadu's Ramanathapuram district—Sakkarakottai and Therthangal—have been designated as Ramsar sites.
 
• With this addition, Tamil Nadu now has 20 Ramsar sites, maintaining the highest number of Ramsar sites in India.
 
• Uttar Pradesh follows with 10 Ramsar sites.
 
• **The new Ramsar sites are:**
 
 
• Sakkarakottai Bird Sanctuary and Therthangal Bird Sanctuary in Tamil Nadu.
 
• Khecheopalri Wetland in Sikkim.
 
• Udhwa Lake in Jharkhand.
 
 
 
• Ramanathapuram already hosts two other Ramsar sites: Chitrangudi and Kanjirankulam.
 
• Tamil Nadu received its first Ramsar designation in 2002 with the Point Calimere Wildlife and Bird Sanctuary.
 
• In 2024, Kazhuveli and Nanjarayan Bird Sanctuaries also received Ramsar status.
 
• **India’s total Ramsar sites now stand at 91, with four new additions: Sakkarakottai, Therthangal, Khecheopalri Wetland (Sikkim), and Udhwa Lake (Jharkhand).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• 
 
 
• 
 Wetland City Accreditation Program

 
 
• Purpose: Recognizes cities for their efforts in conserving wetlands.
 
• Launched: Approved at COP12 of the Ramsar Convention in 2015 (Uruguay).
 
• Objective:
 
• Promote conservation and sustainable use of urban and peri-urban wetlands.
 
• Encourage cities to adopt conservation and restoration measures.
 
 
 
• 
 Accreditation Criteria (6 Key Criteria):

 
 
• Presence of Ramsar Sites or significant wetlands that provide ecosystem services.
 
• Adoption of wetland conservation measures.
 
• Implementation of wetland restoration initiatives.
 
• Integrated spatial/land-use planning for wetlands within the city’s jurisdiction.
 
• Public awareness and participation in wetland conservation.
 
• Establishment of a local committee to support preparation and implementation of measures.
 
• Validity: Accreditation lasts 6 years and can be renewed if criteria continue to be met.
 
• Global Status:
 
• 74 accredited cities globally.
 
• China leads with 22 cities, followed by France (9).
 
 
 
• 
 Ramsar Convention

 
 
• Established: 1971 in Ramsar, Iran; effective from 1975.
 
• Members: 172 countries, including India.
 
• Pillars of the Convention:
 
• Wise use of all wetlands.
 
• Designation and management of Wetlands of International Importance (Ramsar Sites).
 
• International cooperation on transboundary wetland systems.
 
• India’s Ramsar Sites:
 
• India has 91 Ramsar Sites.
 
• Tamil Nadu leads with 18 sites, followed by Uttar Pradesh (10).
 
 
 
• 
 Montreux Record

 
 
• Definition: A record of Ramsar Sites where ecological character has been or is being impacted due to human activities (pollution, development, etc.).
 
• Sites in India on Montreux Record:
 
• Keoladeo National Park
 
• Loktak Lake
 
 
 
 
 
• Amrit Dharohar Initiative__
 
 
• Launched as part of the 2023-24 budget, the initiative focuses on the conservation and sustainable use of Ramsar Sites, generating employment, and supporting local communities.
 
• The initiative aims to enhance the conservation of wetland species and habitats, promote eco-tourism, and improve livelihoods linked to wetlands.

questions.question: Which type of diseases are targeted under the Intensified Special Screening Campaign launched by the Union Health Ministry, which aims to achieve 100% screening coverage for individuals aged 30 years and above?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Non-Communicable Diseases.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **The Ministry of Health & Family Welfare launched the Intensified Special NCD Screening Campaign to ensure 100% screening of individuals aged 30 years and above for Non-Communicable Diseases (NCDs).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• The campaign runs from 20th February to 31st March 2025.
 
• It aims to screen for prevalent NCDs, including Diabetes, Hypertension, and three common cancers—Oral, Breast, and Cervical.
 
• Implemented under the National Programme for Prevention and Control of Non-Communicable Diseases (NP-NCD).
 
• Door-to-door outreach by trained ASHAs, ANMs, and frontline workers to maximize screening coverage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• What are Non-Communicable Diseases (NCDs)?__

 __
 
• Diseases that are not transmitted from person to person.
 
• Develop due to genetic, lifestyle, and environmental factors.
 
• Examples include Diabetes, Hypertension, Cardiovascular diseases, and Cancers.
 
 
 
• Implementation Strategies__
 __
 
• Door-to-door screening by trained healthcare workers.
 
• Daily monitoring and data updates on the NP-NCD Portal.
 
• Essential medical supplies, including BP monitors and glucometers, made available at healthcare centers.
 
• Regular progress review at the state and national levels.
 
 
 
• Ayushman Bharat Initiative__
 
 
• A flagship healthcare program aimed at providing universal health coverage.
 
• Focuses on preventive healthcare and ensuring quality health services for all.
 
• Ayushman Arogya Mandirs (AAMs) play a key role in the screening drive.

questions.question: What was the total GST revenue collection recorded in January 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1.95 lakh crore rupees.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **In January 2025, the Gross GST revenue collection stood at 1.95 lakh crore rupees.**
 
• **This marks a 12.3% growth compared to January 2024.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• The Central GST (CGST) collection for January 2025 was 36,077 crore rupees.
 
• The State GST (SGST) collection amounted to 44,942 crore rupees.
 
• The Integrated GST (IGST) collection was over 1 lakh crore rupees.
 
• The cess collection stood at 13,412 crore rupees.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Goods and Services Tax (GST)**__

 __
 
• GST is a comprehensive indirect tax levied on the supply of goods and services in India.
 
• It was implemented on July 1, 2017, replacing multiple indirect taxes.
 
• GST is categorized into CGST (Central GST), SGST (State GST), IGST (Integrated GST), and cess.
 
 
 
• **State-wise Growth in GST Collection**__
 __
 
• Ladakh recorded the highest GST growth of 39%.
 
• Nagaland and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands saw a 26% increase in GST revenue.
 
 
 
• **GST Council**__
 
 
• The GST Council is responsible for making decisions on tax rates, exemptions, and revenue sharing.
 
• It is chaired by the Union Finance Minister of India.

questions.question: Which country recently joined the OPEC+ group of oil-producing nations ahead of the UN Climate Summit 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Brazil.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **Brazil has joined OPEC+, a coalition of oil-exporting nations, just months before hosting the UN Climate Summit (COP30) in November 2025.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **OPEC+ consists of 12 OPEC members and 10 non-OPEC oil-producing nations, including Russia, the largest non-OPEC participant.**
 
• Brazil, the world’s seventh-largest oil producer, pumps about 4.3 million barrels per day.
 
• While Brazil will take part in OPEC+ discussions, it will not have binding obligations such as production cuts.
 
• The decision to join OPEC+ has sparked debate, as Brazil is also hosting the UN Climate Summit (COP30), which aims to reduce fossil fuel consumption.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• OPEC+ (Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries Plus)__

 __
 
• Formed to regulate oil production and stabilize global oil markets.
 
• Includes 12 OPEC members and 10 additional oil-producing countries.
 
• Saudi Arabia is OPEC’s largest oil producer, while Russia leads the non-OPEC members.
 
 
 
• OPEC__
 
• 
 __
 
• Headquarters of OPEC: Vienna, Austria.
 
• Secretary General: Haitham al-Ghais.
 
• It was founded in 1960.
 
 
 
• Brazil’s Energy and Environmental Policies__
 __
 
• Brazil’s crude oil became its top export product in 2024, surpassing soy.
 
• President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has promoted economic growth through oil revenue while also working to curb Amazon deforestation.
 
 
 
• UN Climate Summit (COP30)__
 
 
• The annual conference focused on global efforts to combat climate change.
 
• Brazil will host COP30 in November 2025, increasing scrutiny of its fossil fuel policies.
 
• Environmental groups have criticized Brazil’s plans for exploratory drilling near the Amazon.

questions.question: Which Indian institute developed a self-actuating drug delivery system for rheumatoid arthritis treatment?

__
 
• **Researchers from the Institute of Nano Science and Technology (INST) Mohali have developed a self-actuating drug delivery system for targeted **rheumatoid arthritis (RA) treatment**.**

__
 
• **The system uses **microspheres loaded with methotrexate**, releasing the drug only in inflamed joints.**
 
• It minimizes side effects, improves therapeutic outcomes, and reduces the need for frequent dosing.
 
• Uses **polymer-lipid hybrid micro-composites** for high drug encapsulation and enzyme-triggered release.
 
• Animal studies showed reduced **joint swelling, inflammation, and cartilage damage**.

__
 
• **AIIMS Delhi:**__ Premier medical institute conducting research on arthritis and autoimmune diseases.
 
• __**IIT Bombay:**__ Known for biomedical research and nanotechnology applications in healthcare.
 
• __**CSIR-CCMB (Centre for Cellular & Molecular Biology):**__ Focuses on genetic and molecular research in diseases.

questions.question: Recently, India's first indigenous Monkeypox RT-PCR test kit is launched. Which private company developed this kit?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Transasia Bio-Medicals**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India's first indigenous Monkeypox RT-PCR test kit was developed by **Transasia Bio-Medicals**.
 
• The kit is designed to detect the Monkeypox virus through **real-time polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR)**, ensuring high accuracy in diagnosis.
 
• Transasia Bio-Medicals is a leading Indian company in the field of **in-vitro diagnostic (IVD) solutions**, known for its innovation and quality.
 
• This development aligns with India's effort to strengthen its healthcare infrastructure and address emerging infectious diseases like Monkeypox.
 
• Monkeypox is a zoonotic disease caused by the **Monkeypox virus**, a member of the Orthopoxvirus genus in the Poxviridae family.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Monkeypox Virus:**

 
 
• The Monkeypox virus is an Orthopoxvirus, similar to the virus that causes smallpox.
 
• The disease is characterized by fever, rash, and swollen lymph nodes, with occasional severe complications.
 
• Human cases of Monkeypox were first identified in 1970 in the Democratic Republic of Congo.
 
 
 
• **RT-PCR Technology:**
 
 
• RT-PCR stands for Real-Time Polymerase Chain Reaction, a molecular technique used for detecting and quantifying nucleic acids.
 
• It is highly sensitive and specific, making it ideal for diagnosing infectious diseases.
 
• RT-PCR has been widely used during the COVID-19 pandemic and is now adapted for Monkeypox detection.
 
 
 
• **Global Monkeypox Outbreak:**
 
 
• In 2022, Monkeypox cases were reported in non-endemic regions, leading to a global health alert.
 
• The World Health Organization (WHO) declared Monkeypox a public health emergency of international concern.
 
• Efforts are underway worldwide to improve diagnostic tools and vaccines for Monkeypox.
 
 
 
• **Transasia Bio-Medicals:**
 
 
• Founded in 1979, Transasia Bio-Medicals is one of India's largest IVD companies.
 
• It offers diagnostic solutions in areas such as hematology, biochemistry, immunology, and microbiology.
 
• The company has a presence in over 130 countries and continues to invest in innovation to address healthcare challenges.
